extracted.intended_audience: Heads of executive departments and establishments; agency and facility managers implementing federal parking policy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for implementing an OMB draft circular that establishes parking fees, carpooling requirements, and related management actions for Federal installations to reduce subsidized employee parking and encourage transit and carpooling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish fees for use of government parking lots
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft circular intended to establish fees for the use of certain government parking lots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: to discourage subsidized employee parking in an energy-conscious era and to encourage carpooling and transit use. The circular proposes a pricing policy affecting primarily downtown and densely populated suburban Federal facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee basis: fair monthly rental value of the parking space
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular would establish a parking fee at all Federal installations based on the fair monthly rental value of the parking space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The intent is to set a commercially equivalent fee that reflects space costs and acts as an incentive to carpooling and transit use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception threshold: no fee where rental value is less than $10/month
rubrics_metrics.description: Except that in most cases no fee will be charged where the rental value is less than $10.00 per month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exception is intended so that very low-value spaces are not administratively burdened; agencies should apply the threshold in implementing fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set fee level to recover space costs and incentivize behavior but not exceed administrative benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: The intent is to set a fee high enough to recover space costs and act as an incentive to carpooling, yet not so low that administration of a fee system and parking management would totally consume the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance fee magnitude between behavioral incentives/cost recovery and administrative overhead; avoid perverse outcomes where collection costs outweigh revenues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a phase-in period for implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular provides for a phase-in period to help employees and agencies adjust carpooling and financial arrangements as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the phase-in to allow time for alternative commuting arrangements (carpooling, vanpooling, transit) and to mitigate hardship from immediate price changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require affirmative plans to maximize carpooling/vanpooling where parking remains free
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency managers at locations which would continue to provide parking without charge will be required to develop and implement affirmative plans for maximizing carpooling and vanpooling among employees and other building tenants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where agencies retain free parking (e.g., below the $10 threshold), they must nonetheless take active measures to increase shared-ride commuting among occupants.

rubrics_metrics.name: More stringent application of carpooling requirements government-wide
rubrics_metrics.description: More stringent application of carpooling requirements will affect all locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniform enforcement of carpooling regulations is expected; surveys showed inconsistent application across installations, so the circular emphasizes strengthening enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired outcomes and metrics: cost savings, energy reduction, congestion reduction, transit use, air quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerable cost savings to the taxpayer, reduced energy consumption, less traffic congestion, increased transit use, greater carpooling and improved air quality are expected from this action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the policy objectives against which implementation success should be measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use commercially equivalent pricing to reduce single-occupant vehicle use
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies (e.g., MWCOG and comparative study in Los Angeles) conclude that charging commercially equivalent fees for parking would reduce the number of cars in the core and increase carpooling and transit use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt market-comparable pricing where appropriate to change commuter behavior; empirical support is cited to justify pricing approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize targeted applicability: downtown and densely populated suburban emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: The pricing policy will primarily affect Federal facilities in downtown locations and densely populated suburban locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation priorities and intensity may be greater in urban cores where commercial-equivalent pricing is most likely to change commuting patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider employee hardship and mitigation strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: In the vast majority of cases, charging a commercial rate for parking is not expected to impose a hardship. In many cases employees will be able to share the costs through carpooling. In other cases, the daily use of public transit may be a more cost effective option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess potential hardships and promote mitigation (carpools, vanpools, transit, phase-in); ensure policy does not unduly burden employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicit written comments by a stated deadline as part of rule/draft process
rubrics_metrics.description: Attached for review is a draft circular; we invite your written comments and ask that they be sent to Ms. Joyce Walker, Deputy Associate Director, Room 9202, OMB, Washington, D.C. 20503, no later than April 30, 1979.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified comment submission procedure and deadline when responding to the draft circular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carpool utilization objective referenced (90% utilization target)
rubrics_metrics.description: Despite the regulation's objective of 90 percent utilization by carpools, GSA survey showed over a third of executive branch parking spaces in the D.C. core were still used by single-occupant vehicles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 90% utilization objective as a benchmark for carpooling performance and identify gaps revealed by surveys to inform stronger application of requirements.
